text: various anthracycline- and taxane-based regimens are in use,3,8 along with newer combinations, such as gemcitabine plus paclitaxel, vinorelbine plus epirubicin, or paclitaxel plus bevacizumab.3 Ixabepilone with or without capecitabine, is another option.3,47 In patients with HER2-overexpress- ing tumours, trastuzumab may be added to chemothera- py:3 the combination is markedly more effective in this group than chemotherapy alone,42 although use with an- thracyclines may be problematic because of the increased risk of cardiotoxicity.3 Higher response rates have been achieved by intensive regimens, combined with autologous bone marrow trans- plants or stem cells in some studies. However, the results of randomised trials have been disappointing, and a sys- tematic review found no improvement in overall survival with the use of stem-cell supported high-dose therapy in metastatic breast cancer.48 The use of bisphosphonates in women with bone metastas- es reduces bone pain and skeletal complications such as fracture, spinal cord compression, and hypercalcaemia (see Malignant Neoplasms of the Bone, above). Radio- therapy is also used for bone pain, and for the treatment of brain metastases (see Malignant Neoplasms of the Brain, above). 1. Hortobagyi GN. Treatment of breast cancer.
